### Problem: Distinct subsequences {#sec-st-p3-dist}

::: {.p-statement}
Return the number of distinct subsequences of `s` that equal `t`. Two subsequences differ when their index sets differ.

$1 \le |s|, |t| \le 1000$. The answer fits in a 32-bit signed integer; cells in the middle may not. On `rabbbit` and `rabbit` the answer is 3: three choices of which `b` to delete. On `babgbag` and `bag` the answer is 5.

Source: [LC 115 · Distinct Subsequences](https://leetcode.com/problems/distinct-subsequences/){.solved difficulty="Hard"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
The first-occurrence greedy finds one embedding and stops. On `babgbag` / `bag` it reports 1, and there are 5. The last letter of `s` is either unused, which keeps the same target, or it matches the last letter of `t`, which shortens both. Those two families are disjoint and cover every embedding.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
- **State.** $dp[i][j]$ = ways to form $t[0..j)$ as a subsequence of $s[0..i)$.
- **Transition.** Always $dp[i - 1][j]$. If $s[i - 1] = t[j - 1]$, also add $dp[i - 1][j - 1]$.
- **Base.** $dp[i][0] = 1$, $dp[0][j] = 0$ for $j > 0$. **Answer.** $dp[n][m]$.
- **One row.** Sweep $j$ from the right, so $dp[j - 1]$ is still the previous row when a match adds it.
:::

The buttons are in order. Each one keeps the previous solution and changes only what that form changes.

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Recursion

::: {.form-next}
`f(i, j)` counts ways to form the suffix of `t` starting at `j` from the suffix of `s` starting at `i`. An empty target has one way. An empty source with a non-empty target has none. Skip the letter, and match it when it equals the next target letter.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("dist", "rec")
    assert str(final) == "3"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-dist-rec
def dist_rec(s, t):
    def f(i, j):
        if j == len(t):
            return 1
        if i == len(s):
            return 0
        ways = f(i + 1, j)
        if s[i] == t[j]:
            ways += f(i + 1, j + 1)
        return ways
    return f(0, 0)
```

##### C++

```cpp
int distRec(int i, int j, const string& s, const string& t) {
    if (j == (int)t.size()) return 1;
    if (i == (int)s.size()) return 0;
    int ways = distRec(i + 1, j, s, t);
    if (s[i] == t[j]) ways += distRec(i + 1, j + 1, s, t);
    return ways;
}
```
:::

#### Memo

::: {.form-next}
The pair `(i, j)` is the whole state. If fewer letters remain in `s` than in `t`, the answer is 0 and the call stops.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("dist", "memo")
    assert str(final) == "3"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-dist-memo
def dist_memo(s, t):
    memo = {}

    def f(i, j):
        if j == len(t):
            return 1
        if i == len(s) or len(s) - i < len(t) - j:
            return 0
        if (i, j) not in memo:
            ways = f(i + 1, j)
            if s[i] == t[j]:
                ways += f(i + 1, j + 1)
            memo[i, j] = ways
        return memo[i, j]

    return f(0, 0)
```

##### C++

```cpp
long long distMemo(int i, int j, const string& s, const string& t, vector<vector<long long>>& memo) {
    if (j == (int)t.size()) return 1;
    if (i == (int)s.size() || (int)s.size() - i < (int)t.size() - j) return 0;
    if (memo[i][j] >= 0) return memo[i][j];
    long long ways = distMemo(i + 1, j, s, t, memo);
    if (s[i] == t[j]) ways += distMemo(i + 1, j + 1, s, t, memo);
    return memo[i][j] = ways;
}
```
:::

#### Table

::: {.form-next}
Column 0 is 1. Every other cell copies the cell above, and adds the diagonal when the letters match. Use a wide integer: a middle cell can be a binomial coefficient far larger than the corner.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("dist", "tab")
    assert str(final) == "3"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-dist-tab
def dist_tab(s, t):
    n, m = len(s), len(t)
    dp = [[0] * (m + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    for i in range(n + 1):
        dp[i][0] = 1
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        for j in range(1, m + 1):
            dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j]
            if s[i - 1] == t[j - 1]:
                dp[i][j] += dp[i - 1][j - 1]
    return dp[n][m]
```

##### C++

```cpp
int distTab(const string& s, const string& t) {
    int n = s.size(), m = t.size();
    vector<vector<unsigned long long>> dp(n + 1, vector<unsigned long long>(m + 1));
    for (int i = 0; i <= n; ++i) dp[i][0] = 1;
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i)
        for (int j = 1; j <= m; ++j) {
            dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j];
            if (s[i - 1] == t[j - 1]) dp[i][j] += dp[i - 1][j - 1];
        }
    return (int)dp[n][m];
}
```
:::

#### One row

::: {.form-next}
`dp[j]` starts as the previous row. Scanning `j` downward, `dp[j]` is still the skip (the old value) and `dp[j - 1]` is still the previous row's diagonal. A match adds that diagonal into `dp[j]`. Left to right would add a value this row already updated, and one letter of `s` would be used twice.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("dist", "row")
    assert str(final) == "3"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-dist-row
def dist_row(s, t):
    dp = [1] + [0] * len(t)
    for ch in s:
        for j in range(len(t), 0, -1):
            if ch == t[j - 1]:
                dp[j] += dp[j - 1]
    return dp[-1]

assert dist_rec("rabbbit", "rabbit") == dist_memo("rabbbit", "rabbit") == 3
assert dist_tab("rabbbit", "rabbit") == dist_row("rabbbit", "rabbit") == 3
assert dist_tab("babgbag", "bag") == dist_row("babgbag", "bag") == 5
assert dist_row("abc", "") == 1 and dist_row("", "a") == 0
```

##### C++

```cpp
int distRow(const string& s, const string& t) {
    int m = t.size();
    vector<unsigned long long> dp(m + 1);
    dp[0] = 1;
    for (char ch : s)
        for (int j = m; j >= 1; --j)
            if (ch == t[j - 1]) dp[j] += dp[j - 1];
    return (int)dp[m];
}
```
:::

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Recursion** branches on every skip. **Memoisation** and the **table** are $O(nm)$. **One row** is $O(nm)$ time and $O(m)$ memory. $|s|, |t| \le 1000$. Store intermediate cells in a 64-bit unsigned integer even though the corner fits in 32 bits: $\binom{40}{20}$ already exceeds $2^{31}$.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- `t` empty: one way, the empty subsequence. The loops never run and `dp[0]` stays 1.
- `s` shorter than `t`: the answer is 0.
- Every letter of `t` has only one place in `s`: the answer is 1.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- Counting distinct strings. `rabbbit` against `rabbit` has one string and three position sets. The answer is 3.
- Sweeping the rolling row left to right. The match then reads a `dp[j - 1]` that already includes the current letter of `s`.
- A 32-bit cell. The corner is small. A middle binomial coefficient is not.
:::

**Variants.** Pairs of equal subsequences, one from each of two integer arrays, including the empty pair, is this grid with a subtraction so that a skipped pair is not counted twice: [AC abc130_e · Common Subsequence](https://atcoder.jp/contests/abc130/tasks/abc130_e). A substring of one string paired with a subsequence of the other is the same addition, restarted at every start position of the substring: [CF 163A · Substring and Subsequence](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/163/A){rating="1700"}.
